visual_goal: Show a rooftop's value to the group as several revenue lines from different invoices converging into one total that needs one customer key and one meter.
prompt: A left-to-right convergence illustration. Far left, a small generic dealership building labeled 'Rooftop'. Four separate arrows fan out from it to the right into four small boxes stacked vertically: 'Modules', 'Data usage', 'Register transactions', 'Finance referral'. Each of the four boxes sends one arrow right into a single large coin-stack box labeled 'Group revenue per rooftop'. One arrow from that box right into a final box showing one key and one gauge meter icon, labeled 'One key, one meter'. These seven labels are the only words in the image.
alt: A rooftop produces four revenue lines (modules, data usage, register transactions, finance referral) that converge into group revenue per rooftop, which needs one key and one meter.

visual_goal: Show that the same stock lifecycle events feed the dealer's KPIs and, via usage events, the platform's meter and invoices.
prompt: A horizontal timeline track across the middle with five rounded event markers from left to right: 'Stock-in', 'Recon', 'First advert', 'Sold', 'Register'. Above the track, two thin bracket arcs: a long one from 'Stock-in' to 'Sold' labeled 'days-to-turn', and a shorter one from 'First advert' to 'Sold' labeled 'days listed'. From 'Sold', one arrow up-right to a teal dashboard box labeled 'Dealer KPIs'. Below the track, a single orange gauge meter box labeled 'Meterline', receiving exactly two arrows: one single diagonal arrow from 'Recon' down into it, and one single diagonal arrow from 'Register' down into it. One arrow from 'Meterline' right to an invoice sheet box labeled 'Invoice and cost'. These ten labels are the only words in the image.
alt: Stock-in, recon, first advert, sold and register events on a timeline; days-to-turn and days listed span to sold, sold feeds dealer KPIs, and recon and register send usage to Meterline, which produces invoice and cost.

visual_goal: Show that a call's margin is decided by whether the license permits reuse and by the result class, both recorded before rating.
prompt: A top-to-bottom flow. At the top, a request envelope box labeled 'Billable request'. One arrow down to a shield-and-document box labeled 'License check'. From it, one arrow down to a diamond decision shape labeled 'Reusable?'. From the diamond, one arrow to the lower left labeled 'yes' into a green box with a cache drawer icon labeled 'Cached answer', and one arrow to the lower right labeled 'no' into an orange box with a euro coin icon (euro sign) labeled 'Paid source'. Both boxes send one arrow down into one box with four small colored dots labeled 'Result class'. One arrow down to a gauge box labeled 'Rating'. One arrow down to a final box with a small rising bar chart labeled 'Margin per call'. These ten labels are the only words in the image.
alt: A billable request passes a license check and a reuse decision: reusable answers come from cache, others from a paid source; both record a result class before rating produces margin per call.
